title: JavaScript Security Core Check
description: Check your understanding of XSS prevention, CSRF, validation and sanitization, token storage, CORS, dangerous code patterns, dependency hygiene, secrets, and safe errors.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of assigning untrusted user input to `innerHTML`?

options.text: The browser may parse the value as HTML and executable content
The value is always converted to a number
The page can no longer use CSS
The request method changes to POST

questions.explanation: `innerHTML` parses a string as HTML. Untrusted strings can change page structure or behavior if rendered this way.

questions.prompt: Which DOM API is usually safest when displaying plain user-provided text?
questions.explanation: `textContent` treats the value as text instead of parsing it as HTML.

options.text: Checks whether a value is acceptable according to rules

questions.explanation: Validation accepts or rejects data based on rules such as type, length, format, or allowed values.

options.text: Cleans, normalizes, or limits a value before use
Proves the user is logged in
Turns every request into a GET request

questions.explanation: Sanitization transforms data, such as trimming an email or removing unsafe markup. It does not replace validation.

questions.prompt: Why is frontend-only validation not enough for important security rules?

options.text: Users can bypass or modify frontend code and call the server directly
Frontend validation only works with CSS

questions.explanation: Frontend validation helps user experience, but the server must enforce important rules because clients are not trusted.

options.text: Unwanted authenticated requests sent by a browser
A syntax error in an arrow function

questions.explanation: CSRF targets the browser's automatic credential behavior, especially with cookie-based sessions.

questions.prompt: Which cookie flag prevents JavaScript from reading a cookie?
questions.explanation: `HttpOnly` cookies are sent by the browser but are not exposed through JavaScript APIs.

questions.prompt: Why can storing sensitive bearer tokens in `localStorage` be risky?

options.text: JavaScript running on the page can read `localStorage`
Browsers publish `localStorage` values in search results

questions.explanation: If malicious or vulnerable code runs on the page, it may be able to read tokens stored in `localStorage`.

options.text: Whether browser JavaScript can read a cross-origin response
Whether a user is an administrator

questions.explanation: CORS is a browser-enforced read boundary for cross-origin responses. It is not authentication.

questions.prompt: Which statement about frontend secrets is correct?

options.text: Private secrets should not be bundled into browser JavaScript
Environment variables are always private in frontend code

questions.explanation: Frontend code is visible to users, so private secrets must stay on the server.

questions.prompt: Why should `eval()` be avoided with untrusted input?

options.text: It runs a string as JavaScript code
It validates all input too strictly

questions.explanation: `eval()` executes strings as code, which is dangerous when the string is influenced by untrusted data.

questions.prompt: What is a good habit before adding a new dependency?

options.text: Check whether a built-in API or existing project package already solves the problem

questions.explanation: Every dependency adds code and maintenance risk. Prefer built-in APIs or existing dependencies when they fit.
